name: Fort Lafayette (Fort Diamond)
shape_note: Square casemated island fort (about 61 m a side, open parade), traced on the USGS The Narrows 1:24,000 sheet of 1955 (photographs 1954), +-10 m; begun 1812, completed 1822, demolished 1960; height estimated (three tiers).

name: Fort Gansevoort (White Fort)
shape_note: In use 1812-1849, demolished 1854 (the article's coordinates); size, shape, height and material estimated.

name: Fort Washington (Fort Knyphausen)
shape_note: Pentagonal earthwork of 1776 on the site of Bennett Park (West 183rd-185th Street, Fort Washington Avenue); taken 16 November 1776; end year estimated (the British evacuation); outline and height estimated.

name: Fort Tryon (Forest Hill redoubt)
shape_note: Outwork of Fort Washington (16 November 1776), named Fort Tryon by the British; end year, position within the park, outline and height estimated.

name: Fort Putnam (Fort Greene)
shape_note: Earthwork fort on the hill of today's Fort Greene Park, built under Nathanael Greene (the year 1776 is from the Fort Defiance article's account of Greene's forts, not stated in this one), refortified in the War of 1812 as Fort Greene; the hill became Washington Park in 1847 (end year = the park); outline and height estimated.

name: Fort Defiance (Red Hook)
shape_note: Redoubt of 1776 at today's Conover and Van Dyke Streets; end year (the British evacuation), outline and height estimated.

name: Cobble Hill Fort (Corkscrew Fort; Fort Swift in 1812)
shape_note: Fort on the conical hill at Atlantic Avenue, Pacific and Court Streets; the British cut off its top during the occupation (end year estimated); refortified as Fort Swift in the War of 1812; outline and height estimated.

name: Elmhurst gas tank (north holder, Newtown Holder Station)
shape_note: Holder 200 ft tall (cited); circle of 84 m read on the USGS Brooklyn 1:24,000 sheet of 1956, +-10 m; the pair was built between 1910 and 1921 - which holder came first is estimated; dismantling began 1996.

name: Elmhurst gas tank (south holder, Newtown Holder Station)
shape_note: Holder 200 ft tall (cited); circle of 84 m read on the USGS Brooklyn 1:24,000 sheet of 1956, +-10 m; start year estimated (the pair was built between 1910 and 1921); dismantling began 1996.

name: Gas holder, Gas House District (Consolidated Gas)

name: Goldwater Memorial Hospital (Welfare Hospital for Chronic Diseases)
shape_note: Opened July 1939, closed 2013 (demolition year 2014 estimated); the chevron pavilions as drawn on the USGS Central Park 1:24,000 sheet of 1966 (ink vectorised by tools/trace_ink.py), +-10 m; height estimated.

name: City Hospital (Charity Hospital)
shape_note: Renwick's hospital completed 1861, closed 1957, demolished 1994; the main building as drawn on the USGS Central Park 1:24,000 sheet of 1966 (ink vectorised by tools/trace_ink.py), +-10 m; height estimated.

name: Blackwell's Island Penitentiary
shape_note: Opened 3 August 1830; the inmates left and the jail was demolished by 1936, Goldwater hospital taking the ground; position, footprint and height estimated.

name: Pearl Street Station (Edison Electric Illuminating Company)
shape_note: 255-257 Pearl Street on a lot of 50 by 100 ft (cited); generating from 4 September 1882, burned 1890 and rebuilt, decommissioned 1895 (end = that year; the building's demolition was not researched); orientation, height and material estimated.

name: Waterside Generating Station (Nos. 1 and 2, switch house)
shape_note: No. 1 (38th-39th Street) October 1901, No. 2 (39th-40th Street) November 1906, offices and switch house on 40th-41st Street; decommissioned 2005 (demolition year estimated); outline: today's empty superblock between First Avenue and the FDR Drive, 38th to 41st Street, which the plant filled (the plant's own walls were not traced); height estimated.

name: St. John's Park Freight Depot (Hudson River Railroad)
shape_note: Four-acre depot on the former park: construction began 1867 (start 1868 estimated: the opening), demolished 1927; footprint from the 4 acres, storeys and height estimated.

name: Havemeyers & Elder sugar refinery (first)
shape_note: First Williamsburg refinery of 1856, replaced by the complex built 1882-83 on the west side of Kent Avenue between South 2nd and South 6th Streets; footprint, height and material estimated.

name: Pavilion of Fun (Steeplechase Park)
shape_note: Steel-and-glass hall of 450 by 280 ft (cited), opened in the 1908 season, demolished September 1966; position inside the park, orientation and height estimated.

name: Dreamland tower (Beacon Tower)
shape_note: Tower 375 ft high (cited; some sources 370 ft), opened 15 May 1904, burned 27 May 1911; position (the article's coordinates of the park), footprint and material estimated.
